newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Italian troops narrowly avoid Albania gunbattle.
newsitem.headline: Italian troops narrowly avoid Albania gunbattle.

text.p: Italian troops patrolling the southern Albanian town of Vlore, the centre of rioting earlier this year, came close to a gunbattle on Tuesday with some of the armed bands roaming the region.

A spokesman for the Italian-led UN-backed multinational force that is protecting aid supplies said Italian soldiers in an armoured personnel carrier watched as two cars chased each other and men in one of the cars opened fire on the other.
Spokesman Lieutenant Colonel Paolo Bianchi said the Italian troops stopped to see how the battle developed but were not forced to open fire.
The mandate of the force says troops are not allowed to disarm civilians but can shoot back if fired at.

Although the violence and rioting of February and March has died down, sporadic violence continues throughout Albania, which slid into chaos after a string of shady investment schemes collapsed, depriving tens of thousands of their life savings.
The incidents are fuelled by the free availability of weapons, with unofficial estimates saying around one million guns were looted from state arsenals during the rioting.
Some residents say many of the weapons have fallen into the hands of criminal bands, who use them to settle scores and fight out battles over territory.
Vlore was last week the scene of several killings, including a gun battle on Saturday in which two died.
